New this week · Tuesday, June 17

Building a tool library
from a single
donated drill.

A conversation with Marcus Haines, founder of Foundry Row

Marcus spent four years turning a rented Oakland garage into a tool-lending nonprofit serving four East Bay neighborhoods. We talk about the slow part — the part nobody photographs — and the suggestion from a single member that quietly reshaped the entire model.

What eighteen years of beekeeping taught me about risk

The economist who quit to make hand-thrown teacups

with Hideo Maruyama, potter

Hideo spent eleven years modeling supply chains at the World Bank. He now sells teacups at a Berkeley farmers' market for $48 each. He thinks he's still doing economics.

About the show

Patience is a production value.

I started Slow Burn Stories in the spring of 2022 because I was tired of interviews that felt like they were on a schedule. I'd spent eight years as a magazine editor — every conversation timed, every quote pre-approved, every story polished until it lost the part I actually liked.

So I built a studio in my garage, bought one good microphone, and started calling people whose work I admired. The deal was simple: an hour minimum. No promo cycle, no book to plug, no clock. Just the long version of whatever they wanted to tell me.

Three years and 64 episodes in, the deal has held. Thank you for being here.

— Cassia
